From the North Salt Lake refineries to the Magna motor plant: sorting SNT-TC-1A from NAS 410 in Salt Lake City

Salt Lake City's NDT work divides along the Wasatch Front. North of downtown, five refineries in North Salt Lake and Woods Cross run on pressure-equipment codes. West and south of the city, Boeing's Salt Lake plant makes composite structures for commercial aircraft, including 787 tail parts, and Northrop Grumman's Magna site produces rocket motors and composite structures. Farther out, the Promontory site in Box Elder County builds large solid rocket motors for Northrop Grumman, L3Harris and other defense suppliers work along the valley, and Hill Air Force Base anchors the north. The two groups certify technicians under different documents.

The refinery corridor

Marathon, Chevron, HF Sinclair and Big West inspect vessels, piping and tanks under ASME and API documents, which look to ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189. Turnaround contractors certify their technicians under SNT-TC-1A written practices, and API inspectors of record sign for the equipment. NAS 410 plays no part on that side of the valley. Plenty of Salt Lake technicians start on turnarounds and later look west toward Magna or Boeing's plant; that move, not a change of course provider, is when NAS 410 enters the picture.

Composite aerostructures and rocket motors

Aerostructure and propulsion plants work inside aerospace and defense contracts. Commercial airframe customers commonly invoke NAS 410 or EN 4179 in supplier purchase orders, and defense subcontracts commonly carry NAS 410 down from the prime, a habit that dates from NAS 410 replacing MIL-STD-410. Under a NAS 410 clause the employer certifies inspectors through a written practice approved by its Responsible Level 3 (RL3), and auditors from customers and Nadcap AC7114 check the files. Where a program's requirements allow an aerospace written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, the plant can use one; the contract decides, not the technician. Composite UT for porosity and bond lines, and radiography of motor hardware, are the signature methods here, so expect method-specific training on the plant's own procedures and parts.

Moving off refinery row: four questions for the RL3

  1. Which standard and revision does your written practice cite, and has it moved to NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025?
  2. Which of my SNT-TC-1A training hours and logged experience will you credit, and in which methods?
  3. How much formal penetrant and magnetic particle training will I need? NAS 410 expects more than SNT-TC-1A recommends.
  4. Will my general, specific and practical examinations use your parts and procedures, and who grades them?

Whatever the answers, keep copies of outlines, hours, signed experience logs, examination results and vision records. An SNT-TC-1A certificate does not meet a NAS 410 requirement on its own; the evidence behind it is what gets credited. If composite work is the goal, the aviation ultrasonic testing guide shows how laminate and bond-line inspection differs from weld UT.

For Wasatch Front suppliers

Machine, composite and bonding shops that sell to the primes often serve mining and industrial customers too. If you certify under both schemes, write the standard and revision on every certification and keep training evidence to the NAS 410 level so it supports either one. Atlantis provides NAS 410 audit documentation support in Salt Lake City: we prepare and review the records a customer or Nadcap auditor will trace, and your RL3 approves them.

Where Atlantis fits along the Wasatch Front

Aerospace, defense and refinery employers in Salt Lake City get the same Atlantis offer: ASNT NDT Level III consulting, SNT-TC-1A-based training, and UT, MT, PT and VT inspection. Our consulting for aerospace companies covers written practices on SNT-TC-1A aligned with customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114, procedures, Level I and II examinations and outside agency ASNT Level III work. Training is self-paced online with Level III questions answered, plus Practical NDT simulator rehearsal and the practical at the employer's facility; there is no Atlantis classroom in Salt Lake City. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Salt Lake City employers. Ask your RL3 whether outside training will count toward NAS 410 certification before you enroll anywhere. For the full picture, read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A and ASNT Level III preparation, and see the Ogden page for Hill AFB work.
